title: Compliance request caseflow and residency-evidence automation
creator: Anjali Rao
description:
Problem: Enterprise buyers repeatedly submit ad-hoc compliance requests asking for: (1) proof of data residency for a tenant or dataset, (2) retention policy snapshots for a given date range, and (3) signed DPA or contractual artifacts. Current handling is manual: SEs aggregate logs, compliance team pulls S3 exports, legal sends DPA PDFs, and we track requests in Sheets/Support tickets. This is slow, error-prone, and blocks deals.

Scope: Build an integrated 'Compliance Caseflow' in the Console and an accompanying API that lets customers open a compliance request, auto-collect evidence artifacts (residency certs, retention config snapshots, audit logs, KMS key metadata, DPA link), run a questionnaire template (SaaS security + data processing questions) and produce a downloadable evidence bundle (PDF/ZIP) with signed DPA status. The feature will include: (a) Questionnaire templates with branching logic and saved responses; (b) Data residency validator that queries our infra layer and returns region provenance; (c) Retention snapshot generator showing active retention rules and recent deletions/events; (d) One-click export that compiles logs, config, and signed legal artifacts; (e) Webhook/API and ServiceNow/Zendesk integration for tracking; (f) RBAC to restrict access to evidence downloads.

Goals & success metrics: 
- Reduce average compliance request turnaround time from ~7 business days to <24 hours for standard requests.
- Reduce manual SE/compliance hours per request by 80%.
- Increase self-serve requests completed by customers to 60% of incoming requests within 90 days of release.
- Generate automated evidence bundles with <2% missing-critical-artifact rate in first quarter.

Out of scope for MVP: Fully automated legal negotiation of DPAs, per-customer custom retention-remediation actions, on-prem air-gapped artifact collection (will be tracked as Private deployment work).

User stories: 
- As a Security Reviewer at a customer, I want to run a standard SOC-like questionnaire and get answers and artifacts so I can complete an intake without emailing Redwood.
- As an Account Executive, I want to trigger a 'compliance bundle' and attach it to a proposal to accelerate procurement.
- As an internal Compliance Analyst, I want the system to flag missing artifacts and queue manual follow-ups with links to the exact logs and PRs.

Trade-offs & decisions made so far: 
- Console-first with an API: build UX in Console for discoverability, but expose the same flow over API for programmatic integrations.
- Evidence storage: store short-lived bundles in S3 with signed URLs (30 days) rather than permanently storing PDFs to limit long-term exposure and simplify retention controls. Legal prefers retention-limited access; infra supports ephemeral bundles.
- Questionnaire versioning: adopt a semantic template version ID to allow audits to reference the template used when evidence was generated.

Acceptance criteria: (see acceptance_criteria field)

Open questions: 
- Law/legal has requested proof of signature chain for DPAs (electronic signing provider selection). Need Legal + Procurement to confirm provider by 2026-03-20.
- For Private deployments, how will evidence extraction work when control plane cannot access tenant storage? Engineering to propose a secure connector pattern by 2026-03-31.

acceptance_criteria: Console: user can create a new compliance request and select a questionnaire template and evidence types (residency, retention, logs, DPA status)
API: /v1/compliance_requests accepts request payload and returns request id and status URL
Evidence bundle: generated ZIP includes manifest.json, questionnaire-responses.json, retention-snapshot.txt, residency-report.txt, links to signed DPA and export log
RBAC: only users with compliance_download role can download evidence bundles
Integrations: webhook delivery to customer-specified URL and Zendesk ticket creation with link to bundle
Observability: metrics emitted for time-to-bundle, missing-artifact rate, and request volume
